title: Inside a Server
summary: Explore the different computer components that help a server process, store, and communicate information.
objectives: Identify the conceptual roles of common server components.
Explain why a server needs both computing parts and a network connection.

vocab.def: One part of a larger device or system.
The part that carries out instructions and calculations.
Fast working space used while a computer is doing tasks.

sections.heading: Different parts have different jobs
sections.body: A processor, or CPU, carries out instructions. Memory holds working information for quick use. Storage keeps information for later. A motherboard connects parts so they can communicate.

sections.heading: Power and connection matter too
sections.body: A power supply provides the kind of power a server needs, while a network connection lets it communicate with other systems. A server is useful because these parts work together.

sections.heading: Learn with models
sections.body: A labeled paper diagram or classroom computer model is a safe way to study components. Do not open energized equipment or attempt repairs; professional hardware work requires qualified supervision.

practice.prompt: Match the need to a component: carry out instructions, hold working information, keep information, or connect parts.

quiz.question: Which component carries out computer instructions?

reflectionPrompt: Which server component role was easiest to explain, and which one would you like to investigate further?
